entities.summary:
Khamudi was the last ruler of the Fifteenth Dynasty of Egypt, reigning from 1534 BC or 1541 BC. His capital, Avaris, was a significant urban center during the Second Intermediate Period.

Khamudi's short reign was marked by his defeat at the hands of Ahmose I, which led to the end of the dynasty and the beginning of the New Kingdom period. This event had significant consequences for the region, including the eventual unification of Egypt under a single ruler.

The legacy of Khamudi can be seen in the cultural and historical context of ancient Egypt, where he played a key role in shaping the country's politics and society during a time of great change.

 Ahmose I, the victor, would go on to become one of the most famous pharaohs of ancient Egypt, and his reign marked the beginning of a new era of Egyptian history.
